evidence.note: Tracked aggregate '776/780 with 4 failing compile cases' and enumerated the specific failing tests by suite, using the list to decide what to fix next.
Noticed 'A new gcc_torture compile failure appears at 20010129-1' after its previous change — awareness of a failure emerging.

Diagnosed that its own dg-options extraction introduced an incompatible flag causing the failure and fixed it, tracking count down to 'Only one test remains failing' — genuine self-introduced-regression detection.
Confirmed final per-suite breakdown (146/146, 221/221, 413/413, 780/780) by re-running the full suite to verify net progress.

reasoning: The agent went beyond mere aggregate counts (level 5): it maintained a current picture of which specific tests failed per suite, re-ran the full suite after each change to confirm net progress, and caught a regression it introduced via its dg-options change (steps 10-12), then reported a per-suite final breakdown. However, it kept no maintained structured ledger by feature, the horizon was very short, and regression detection was incidental to full-suite reruns rather than a deliberate ongoing watch, so it falls short of the sustained, structured process at level 8.
